# Initial Functions

### Simulate one null data set

**inputs**

+ `t`: the maximum time
+ `timestep`: the time increments
+ `mu`: the original mean of the distribution
+ `sigma`: the original standard deviation of the distribution

**outputs**

+ one tibble of `t/timestep` `(time, value)` points generated under the null model

```{r nullPlot-function}
nullPlot <- function(t, timestep, mu, sigma) {
  
  repeat{
    null_data <- tibble(time = seq(1, t, timestep),
                        value = rnorm(t / timestep, mean = mu, sd = sigma)
                        ) |> 
      mutate(value = value - mean(value))
    
    if(max(null_data$value) <= 8*mu & min(null_data$value) >= -8*mu){
      break
    }
  }
  
  return(null_data)
  
}

# test it
# nullPlot(t = 30, timestep = 1, mu = 1, sigma = 1)
```

### Simulate target data set

**inputs**

+ `t`: the maximum time
+ `timestep`: the time increments
+ `cpLoc`: the location (in proportion) along the $x$-axis in which the change occurs
+ `mu`: the original mean of the distribution
+ `theta`: the shift in mean in terms of $\mu(1+\theta)$
+ `sigma`: the original standard deviation of the distribution
+ `gam`: the change in variance (not using this yet)

**outputs**

+ one tibble of `t/timestep` `(time, value)` points generated under the target model

```{r, targetPlot-function}
targetPlot <- function(t, timestep, cpLoc, mu, theta, sigma, gam){
  
  cp = ceiling(t*cpLoc)
  
  repeat{
    target_data <- tibble(time = seq(1, cp, timestep),
         value = rnorm((cp) / timestep, mean = mu, sd = sigma)) |> 
    rbind(
      tibble(time = seq(cp + 1, t, timestep),
             value = rnorm((t - cp) / timestep, mean = mu*(1+theta), sd = sigma*(1+gam)))
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(value = value - mean(value),
                  panel = "target")
    
    if(max(target_data$value) <= 8*mu & min(target_data$value) >= -8*mu){
      break
    }
  }
  
  return(target_data)
  
}
```

### Calculate T-statistic for measuring change point strength

```{r, calcMetrics}

calcMetrics <- function(t, cpLoc, theta, data){
  
  # set up entire data
  target_data <- data
  cp = ceiling(t*cpLoc)
  n  = nrow(target_data)
  
  # setup split values (before cp and after cp)
  x_before    <- as.matrix(target_data[1:cp, "value"])
  x_after    <- as.matrix(target_data[(cp + 1):n, "value"])
  
  # t-test
  ttest <- t.test(x_after, x_before, var.equal = FALSE)

  # output metrics
  tibble(Tstat = ttest$statistic,
         df = n - 2,
         pvalue = ttest$p.value
         )

}

# test it
# target_test <- targetPlot(t = 30, timestep = 1, cpLoc = 0.33, mu = 1, theta = -3, sigma = 1, gam = 0)
# calcMetrics(t = 30, cpLoc = 1/2, theta = -1, data = target_test)
```

### Generate a single lineup data set

**inputs**

+ `t`: the maximum time
+ `timestep`: the time increments
+ `cpLoc`: the location (in proportion) along the $x$-axis in which the change occurs
+ `mu`: the original mean of the distribution
+ `theta`: the shift in mean in terms of $\mu(1+\theta)$
+ `sigma`: the original standard deviation of the distribution
+ `gam`: the change in variance (not using this yet)

**outputs**

+ one tibble of `t/timestep` `(time, value)` points generated under the null model

```{r, lineupData-funciton}

lineupData <- function(t, timestep, cpLoc, mu, theta, sigma, gam){
  
    # expand the grid to generate 19 null data sets given mu and sigma
    null_data <- tibble(panel = "null",
                        mu = mu,
                        sigma   = sigma) |> 
      expand_grid(.n = 1:19) |> 
      dplyr::mutate(data = pmap(list(t = t, timestep = timestep, mu = mu, sigma = sigma), nullPlot)) |> 
      unnest(data) |> 
      select(time, value, panel, .n)
    
    # simulate one target data set given parameters
    target_data <- targetPlot(t = t, timestep = timestep, cpLoc = cpLoc, mu = mu, theta = theta, sigma = sigma, gam = gam)
    
    # calculate metrics on target data set
    metrics <- calcMetrics(t = t, cpLoc = cpLoc, theta = theta, data = target_data)
      
    # randomize the position of the target data
    pos <- sample(1:20, 1)
    
    # randomize the data to panels
    lineup_data <- lineup(true = target_data,
                          samples = null_data,
                          pos = pos) |>
      mutate(obs_plot_location = pos) |>
      nest(data = -pos) |>
      cbind(metrics)
    
    return(lineup_data)

}

# test it
poo <- lineupData(t = 30, timestep = 1, cpLoc = 0.5, mu = 1, theta = -5, sigma = 1, gam = 0)
# lineupData(t = 30, timestep = 1, cpLoc = 0.5, mu = 1, theta = 5, sigma = 2, gam = 0) |>
#   unnest(data) %>%
#   select(value) %>%
#   summary()
```

# Specify parameter's and generate lineup data

Generate 2 versions of lineups for each parameter (A & B).

```{r, parms}
# set up a grid of parameter values to test
parms <- expand_grid(t = 30,
                     timestep = 1,
                     cpLoc = c(1/3, 1/2, 2/3),
                     mu = 1,
                     theta = c(-5, -3, -1, 0, 1, 3, 5),
                     sigma = c(1, 2),
                     gam = 0
)
                               
parms |> knitr::kable(digits = 2)

all_lineups_data <- parms |> 
  expand_grid(version = c("A", "B")) |>
  mutate(lineup = pmap(list(t, timestep, cpLoc, mu, theta, sigma, gam), lineupData)) |> 
  unnest(lineup) |>
  mutate(param_id = paste(round(cpLoc,2), theta, sigma, sep = "_")) |>
  mutate(dataset_id = paste(version, round(cpLoc,2), theta, sigma, sep = "_")) |>
  rowwise() |> 
  mutate(pic_id = digest(paste(version, round(cpLoc,2), theta, sigma, Sys.time(), sep = "_"), "md5"))
```

### Plot & save the lineups

```{r plot-lineups, eval = F}

# digest(paste0(, Sys.time(), sep = ""), "md5", serialize = F)

source("save_lineups.R")

picture_details <- all_lineups_data |>
  select(t, timestep, cpLoc, mu, theta, sigma, gam, version, pos, Tstat, df, pvalue, params, dataset, picid)
write.csv(picture_details, file = "plots/picture_details.csv", row.names = F)

for(i in 1:nrow(all_lineups_data)){
  
  picid <- all_lineups_data[i, "picid"]
  lineup_data <- all_lineups_data[i,c("picid", "data")] |>
                    unnest(data)
  
  # save lineup data set
  write.csv(lineup_data, file = paste0("plots/data/", picid, ".csv"), row.names = F)
  
  lineup_plot <- lineup_data |>
                    ggplot(aes(x = time, y = value)) +
                    theme_bw() +
                    theme(aspect.ratio = 1,
                          axis.text = element_blank()
                          ) +
                    geom_point(color = "blue", size = 0.75) +
                    facet_wrap(~ .sample) +
                    xlab("Time") +
                    ylab("Measured Values") +
                    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-8,8))
  
    save_lineup(lineup_plot, filename = picid, path = "plots", width = 10, height = 8.3, dpi = 600)

}
```
